Solution 1 is the most likely to be correct, but I am not confident that its value of 8 is the true critical degree.

Solution 1 uses the right approach: a two-lineage distance process on the locally tree-like graph, with a search for a bound state below the continuous spectrum edge d − 2√(d−1). Its rates and its factorisation are consistent. At d = 9, for instance, the root u = 3 gives s = 3 and z = 1/2, which satisfy the recurrence.

Its criterion is too weak, though. It only asks whether the discriminant (d−1)(d−9) is non-negative. A genuine bound state also needs a normalisable eigenfunction in the tree-weighted space, which requires z < 1/√(d−1). At d = 9 the root z = 1/2 exceeds 1/√8 ≈ 0.354, so it is not normalisable. A rough check suggests the bound state only appears from about d = 10 onward, so 8 is probably not exact either.

Solution 2 rests on a heuristic Kesten–Stigum threshold of (d−1)/4 = 1, which is not a real derivation. Solution 3 gives no derivation at all and just asserts 3.

Solution 1 is the only one with a coherent spectral argument and the closest value to what my check suggests, so I pick it.

CHOICE: 1
